reason: Non-verticillate means not whorled, so the negated whorled target fits.
Not angular is the negation of angular.
Not marginal is the negation of the marginal position value. I could not read the FLOPO_0991208 definition, so this is less certain.
Not truncate is the negation of truncated.
Smelly only says that a smell is present. It is not necessarily foul, and FLOPO_0991020 is defined as an unpleasant, offensive odour. A plain odour quality is safer.
Basi-dorsifixed means attached by the back at the base. Plain dorsifixed loses the basal position.
Flabellate venation is fan-like. Actinodromous means several primary veins radiating from one point. The two are not the same, so the rule should be rejected.
Ventricose means swollen or bellied, usually in the middle. Gibbous means swollen on one side. Negating a loose synonym is unreliable.
This is a misspelling of anastomosing.
The FLOPO ovate definition is broadest below the middle, towards the base. The match is loose, since the egg-shaped outline is implied rather than stated.
Cobweb-like is the meaning of arachnose.
Filmy means very thin and translucent, which is membranous.
Flesh-coloured means pale pink.
This is a typo for inconspicuous.
Non-beaked is the negation of beaked.
Pinnately nerved is pinnately veined. Nerve and vein are used for the same thing.
Stinking is foetid.
Streaky is streaked.
A tetrahedron is a triangular pyramid, so subtetrahedral is close to pyramidal. The match is approximate.
Wide-angled branching or spreading is divaricate. The match is approximate.
Widest in the middle, with both ends narrowing, is elliptic.
Darker lines on a surface is the streaked pattern.
Tolerant to is relational and needs a stressor. The rule loses that it is drought that is tolerated.
A frayed margin is irregularly torn, which is lacerate.
Leaf-shaped is leaf-like.
Nodeless means the stem has no nodes, so stem node absent is right.
Pulpy means soft and juicy. A part can be fleshy without being pulpy, so not pulpy does not mean not fleshy.
Right-twining names the twining direction (clockwise), and plain climbing loses it. Twining is only one kind of climbing.
String-like is thread-like, which is filiform.
Comose means a terminal tuft of hairs on a seed or fruit. A tuft of hairs on other parts, such as leaf axils or nodes, is not comose.
Biglobular means made of two globose parts. Bilobed means having two lobes.
Connate-perfoliate means the leaf bases are fused and surround the stem. Plain connate loses the perfoliate meaning.
Densely distributed means crowded.
Dust-like means powdery or very fine. It does not mean a decrease in size, because decreased size is relative.
Fringeless means not fringed.
Non-peeling means not exfoliating. Peeling is a listed synonym of exfoliating.
Acuneate is not a standard term, and the rule reads it as cuneate. If it is a negation, it would be not cuneate, and the sense is unclear.
Strigillose is strigulose, which has small, appressed, stiff hairs. Adpressed adds nothing, because strigose hairs are already appressed.
Bark-covered means bark is present.
Brownish buff is a pale tan-brown, close to light brown.
Campaniform is bell-shaped, which is campanulate.
Cinerous means ash-grey.
Cork-like is corky.
Cymose-fasciculate describes a cyme-like arrangement of fascicles. Plain fascicled loses the cymose structure.
A depressed ellipsoid is flattened at the poles, which is an oblate spheroid. The match is approximate.
This is a typo for ellipsoid, and PATO lists ellipsoid as a synonym of elliptic.
Fulcate is a typo for falcate.
Gibberulous is a diminutive of gibbous, meaning slightly swollen on one side.
Half-sheathing means the base partly clasps the stem, like half-amplexicaul. The match is approximate.
Ill-odoured is foul-smelling.
